import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 898

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/898](https://www.erdosproblems.com/898)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Mordell_inequality)
-/

open Affine EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos898

/--
If $A,B,C\in \mathbb{R}^2$ form a triangle and $P$ is a point in the interior then, if $N$ is
where the perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$ meets the triangle, and similarly for $M$ and $L$,
$$
\overline{PA}+\overline{PB}+\overline{PC}\geq 2(\overline{PM}+\overline{PN}+\overline{PL}).
$$

Conjectured by Erdős in 1932 (according to [Er82e]) and proved by Mordell soon afterwards, now
known as the Erdős-Mordell inequality.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos898.lean"]
theorem erdos_898 (A B C P L M N : ℝ²) (hABC : AffineIndependent ℝ ![A, B, C])
    (hP : P ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ ({A, B, C} : Set ℝ²)))
    (hN : N ∈ line[ℝ, A, B]) (hPN : line[ℝ, P, N].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, A, B].direction)
    (hM : M ∈ line[ℝ, B, C]) (hPM : line[ℝ, P, M].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, B, C].direction)
    (hL : L ∈ line[ℝ, C, A]) (hPL : line[ℝ, P, L].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, C, A].direction) :
    dist P A + dist P B + dist P C ≥ 2 * (dist P M + dist P N + dist P L) := by
  sorry

end Erdos898

reformulations.difference: The declaration universally quantifies the perpendicular feet and characterizes them by supporting-line membership and orthogonality of line directions, rather than defining them as orthogonal projections. Triangle nondegeneracy is expressed by affine independence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any P,A,B,N, the two foot hypotheses are equivalent to orthogonalProjection (line[ℝ,A,B]) P = N: the direction of PN is the span of P−N, so its orthogonality is precisely the projection characterization. These projections exist and are unique. AffineIndependent ℝ ![A,B,C] is equivalent to noncollinearity. I proved the full theorem type equivalent to the noncollinear-triangle statement with projection distances in /workspace/review/checks.lean, without using the theorem's sorry. Supporting lines, rather than segments, are correct: Wikipedia explicitly notes that a perpendicular foot may lie outside an obtuse triangle.

sources_consulted: Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved (1982), Chapter I, §1, p. 61: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean; Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean and Orthogonal.lean; Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/AffineSpace/Independent.lean, FiniteDimensional.lean and AffineSubspace/Defs.lean; Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Basic.lean and Hull.lean; Mathlib/Topology/Defs/Basic.lean; Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Affine/AddTorsorBases.lean; Mathlib/Geometry/Euclidean/Projection.lean.
